claims.proposition_evaluated: On August 26, 2026, Infrastructure Committee rejected administration’s recommended hold on the remaining programme routes, and City Council had not adopted that hold by September 25, 2026. I applied the brief’s requirement that a hold expressly defer the listed routes pending a further step.
claims.interpretation_notes: Partially supported: R was not adopted at item 7.6, but the committee did not reject R, and the declared primary Attachment 5, Version 2 (DocumentId 304030), does not expressly say the listed routes must wait for evaluation or Council direction before advancing. Salvador’s incompatible motion to continue the previously approved scope was defeated 2–2; no motion to adopt R was put. The separate privacy motion carried 4–0 and did not decide R. Under the required looser reading of 'did not support', non-adoption makes the classification Supported. City Council as a body: Not established; the available record shows a funding notice laid over to October 6, not a decision on R. An override is not shown: the committee made no substantive decision on R for Council to override. Version 2 is the declared primary because the agenda and minutes list all three versions without identifying which was before members during debate.

supporting_evidence.finding: Infrastructure Committee item 7.6 records no motion adopting Recommendation 1. Rutherford’s amendment to remove accelerated construction language lost 2–2: Rutherford and Clarke in favour; Salvador and Janz opposed. Salvador’s motion to continue the previously approved CM-20-0330 scope, advance tender-ready routes and prepare 2027 procurement then lost 2–2: Salvador and Janz in favour; Rutherford and Clarke opposed. Knack and Paquette, though committee members present during portions of the meeting, cast neither of those votes. Elliott, Morgan, Parmar, Principe, Stevenson, Tang and Wright attended as non-members and could not vote on item 7.6.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The motions, recorded votes and results at the committee meeting.

supporting_evidence.finding: At City Council’s September 8 meeting, item 11.6 was a notice seeking future budget options for the routes listed for reevaluation; it was laid over to October 6. It was not approval of R.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The recorded status of the related notice at Council, not a decision on the administration recommendation.

challenging_evidence.finding: Version 2 says the remaining routes will be evaluated and that administration will bring options to Council in Q1 2027. It does not expressly state that construction or advancement of the 14 listed routes must wait for that report or a Council decision.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The treatment proposed in the declared primary version of R.

challenging_evidence.finding: The only substantive motion put at item 7.6 sought to continue the previously approved scope and was defeated. Its defeat did not adopt a hold or carry a decision incompatible with R.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The committee left R without a substantive decision under the brief’s definitions.

limitations: The portal blocked direct retrieval of its meeting pages and files; I used the complete carried item 7.6 and the carried September 8 Council item. The portal calendar and full September 15 and 22 public-hearing minutes could not be checked for the Council meeting table. The October 6 agenda URL also could not be retrieved.

The agenda and minutes list the original and both replacement versions of Attachment 5 but do not identify the version actually discussed. Version 2 is therefore the brief’s declared primary, with the original and Version 1 reported under claim 2.
unknowns: Whether an uncarried Council item before September 25 referred to R.
Whether committee members discussed R without putting it to a vote; the minutes do not record debate.

missing_evidence.description: Complete Council agendas and minutes through September 25, including the September 15 and 22 public hearings, and the portal meeting calendar.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Office of the City Clerk

what_would_change_my_verdict: Official minutes showing that the committee carried a motion incompatible with R would establish rejection; minutes showing adoption of R by either body would contradict the proposition.
A dated Council decision before September 25 approving the approach would change the Council non-adoption finding.
claims.suggested_one_line: Infrastructure Committee did not adopt administration’s revised approach, but it did not vote it down or vote to continue the old scope; full Council had no documented decision on it by September 25.
claims.suggested_short_answer: At item 7.6, a motion to continue the previously approved programme lost on a 2–2 tie, and nobody put administration’s recommendation to a vote. The operative version is uncertain; the declared Version 2 proposes evaluation and a 2027 report but does not expressly defer the listed routes. Council’s recorded related notice was laid over beyond the review date.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In IS03688, administration recommended approval of an approach expressly deferring construction or advancement of exactly 14 named, unbuilt programme routes until further evaluation, a report or a decision.
claims.interpretation_notes: Partially supported: Recommendation 1 asks for approval of Attachment 5, Version 2 lists 14 routes for possible reevaluation, and Attachment 3 establishes that construction had not started on any of them as of August 10, 2026. The failed element is express deferral: Version 2 says the remaining routes will be evaluated and reported to Council in Q1 2027, but does not say those routes must wait before construction or advancement. Version 2 also fails the stricter 'removed from scope or will not proceed' reading. Version 1 lists the same routes and says they may be revisited; its route-specific passage likewise does not expressly defer all 14 or remove all 14 from scope, so both readings are Partially supported. The original says the 14 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027'; it is Supported under both readings. Classification is version-sensitive. All three versions list 13 entries continuing as planned and 14 listed apart. I counted each bullet as one route; splitting the two entries joined by 'and' and the three-segment Grovenor entry would make 18 listed-apart entries, rather than the attachment’s 14.

supporting_evidence.finding: Recommendation 1 asks Infrastructure Committee to recommend City Council approval of the updated approach in Attachment 5. The report labels the action 'Council decision required' and says the recommendation would require no change to capital profile CM-20-0330 or its borrowing bylaws.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Infrastructure Services report IS03688, pages 1 and 6
supporting_evidence.establishes: What administration recommended, to whom, and its stated budget effect.

supporting_evidence.finding: Version 2 lists these 13 routes as continuing: 50 Street (109A Avenue to Goldbar Park Road); 84 Avenue (Mill Creek Ravine to 91 Street); 100 Street (76 Avenue to 80 Avenue); 107 Avenue (east of Groat Road to 163 Street); 110 Avenue/90 Street and 112 Avenue; 111 Avenue (120 to 121 Street); 114 Avenue (81 to 89 Street); 127 Avenue (97 to 102A Street); 163 Street (87 to 95 Avenue); 163 Street (Stony Plain Road to 107 Avenue); 167/169 Street (Whitemud Drive to 87 Avenue); Kingsway (113 to 122 Street); and Victoria Park Road (116 Street to River Valley Road). It separately lists 14 entries for possible reevaluation.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The two route lists and their counts in the declared primary version.

supporting_evidence.finding: The 14 entries listed apart, identical across all three versions, are 50 Street (101 to 109A Avenue); 64 Street (119 Avenue to Yellowhead Trail); 79 Street (76 to 101 Avenue); 84 Avenue (79 to 83 Street); 85 Street (93 to 98 Avenue); 88 Avenue/93 Street/87 Avenue (85 to 96 Street); 89 Street (76 Avenue to Connors Road); 92A Avenue/86 Street/alley (Connors Road to 85 Street); 93 Street (82 to 84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 to 89 Street); 93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue (85 to 75 Street) and 75 Street (94 to 94B Avenue); 95 Avenue (142 to 163 Street); 101 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); 106 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); and Grovenor: 148 Street, 104 Avenue and 144 Street. The original expressly removes these from programme scope for 2026 and 2027.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The route names, count and treatment in the original version.

supporting_evidence.finding: Attachment 3 dates its statuses August 10. It records the 84 Avenue and 92A Avenue entries as tendered but not started; the 93 Street/84 Avenue entry under a different combined description as tendered but not started; six other entries as formerly scheduled for 2026 but no longer viable for 2026 installation; and the remaining five as having no delivery plan or schedule. None is recorded as under construction or complete.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The listed routes’ reported construction status as of August 10, 2026.

challenging_evidence.finding: Version 2’s operative wording is: 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications. In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report outlining trade-offs and options for the remaining routes, including an update on the remaining funding and budget implications, for Council direction and approval.' Its route list says the projects 'may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.' Neither passage expressly says construction or advancement waits.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The missing express deferral in the declared primary version.

challenging_evidence.finding: Version 1 says the listed projects 'may be revisited using alternate design approaches or other future initiatives.' Its general approach removes routes that affect travel lanes or parking, but does not say every one of the 14 named entries has that effect. The original differs: it says the listed projects 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027.'
challenging_evidence.establishes: Version sensitivity and the limit of Version 1’s route-specific wording.

limitations: The agenda and minutes list all three versions without identifying the version considered during debate; the brief directs use of Version 2 as primary in this circumstance.

Attachment 3’s route-specific statuses are dated August 10, despite appearing with the August 26 report. No dated City record found establishes every route’s individual construction status on August 26.
unknowns: Whether construction started on any listed route between August 10 and August 26.
Whether members relied on the original, Version 1 or Version 2 during deliberation.

missing_evidence.description: A dated August 26 route-by-route construction status and a record identifying the attachment version used at item 7.6.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Infrastructure Services and Office of the City Clerk

what_would_change_my_verdict: An official identification of the original Attachment 5 as the operative version would make this Supported under both deferral readings, subject to the August 10 statuses.
An operative Version 2 passage expressly requiring the 14 routes to wait for evaluation or Council approval would make the primary reading Supported.
claims.suggested_one_line: Administration listed 14 routes for possible reevaluation, all reported unbuilt on August 10; the declared primary attachment does not expressly freeze their construction.
claims.suggested_short_answer: IS03688 sought Council approval of a revised approach. Version 2 lists 13 routes to continue and 14 for possible reevaluation, with a report promised in Q1 2027. The original attachment expressly removed the 14 from scope for 2026 and 2027, so the answer depends on which version was operative.

claims.proposition_evaluated: From the programme’s approval through September 25, 2026, Principe or Rice moved or seconded two defeated City Council motions that would each leave CM-20-0330 with an approved capital budget of $45 million to $55 million and direct the reduction to a named destination.
claims.interpretation_notes: Partially supported: Principe moved and Rice seconded two reductions on separate budget occasions, and both lost. The November 2023 operative motion meets the primary amount band: reviewer calculation, $100,000,000 approved less $50,000,000 equals $50,000,000. The December 2024 motion fails that band: $100,000,000 less $33,650,000 for 2025 less $33,650,000 for 2026 equals $32,700,000. Both specify a reduction in tax-supported debt funding, a named destination under the brief’s rule; the November 2023 preliminary wording also said 'towards the tax levy', but that wording was replaced before the vote. Both meet the alternative 'reduce by at least half' test, yielding Supported under that amount rule. Both also meet the alternative co-sponsorship rule because Principe moved and Rice seconded each. The 2023 Rice/Principe $26,808,000 amendment was withdrawn and did not identify CM-20-0330. Principe seconded Cartmell’s September 2025 motion to cease some bike-lane construction pending review; it lost 4–9 but did not seek a budget reduction.

supporting_evidence.finding: At the November 21–29, 2023 budget meeting, Capital Budget Amendment 2 as put was moved by Principe and seconded by Rice: 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 be reduced by $50,000,000 ($16,350,000 in 2024, $16,825,000 in 2025, and $16,825,000 in 2026) with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt.' Hamilton, Cartmell, Rice and Principe voted in favour; Knack, Paquette, Sohi, Salvador, Tang, Rutherford, Stevenson and Wright opposed. It was defeated 4–8.
supporting_evidence.source_title: City Council budget minutes, November 21–29, 2023, items 5.1.1–5.1.2
supporting_evidence.establishes: The first operative motion, roles, destination, vote and defeat.

supporting_evidence.finding: At the December 2–5, 2024 budget meeting, Capital Budget Amendment 2 was moved by Principe and seconded by Rice: 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 be decreased by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026 with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery of the Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 project.' Cartmell, Rice, Rutherford and Principe voted in favour; Knack, Sohi, Salvador, Janz, Tang, Stevenson and Wright opposed. It was defeated 4–7.
supporting_evidence.source_title: City Council budget minutes, December 2–5, 2024, items 5.1.1–5.1.2
supporting_evidence.establishes: The second operative motion, roles, destination, vote and defeat.

supporting_evidence.finding: Council approved capital profile CM-20-0330 for $100,000,000 during its November 30–December 2022 budget meeting. A City capital financial update for September 30, 2024 still reports a $100,000,000 current approved budget. The later profile records a $430,000 reduction in 2025, after both candidate motions.
supporting_evidence.source_title: City capital financial update, September 30, 2024, Attachment 2
supporting_evidence.establishes: The contemporaneous $100,000,000 capital-budget base for the December 2024 calculation.

challenging_evidence.finding: The December 2024 motion named two $33,650,000 decreases, totaling $67,300,000. Against the $100,000,000 approved capital budget, the reviewer-calculated remainder is $32,700,000, below the primary $45 million–$55 million band.
challenging_evidence.source_title: City Council budget minutes, December 2–5, 2024, item 5.1.2
challenging_evidence.establishes: Why the second motion fails the primary amount requirement.

challenging_evidence.finding: The November 2023 original amendment said the $50,000,000 would go 'towards the tax levy', but Council voted on a restated amendment specifying a reduction from tax-supported debt. The withdrawn Rice/Principe amendment for $26,808,000 was neither a recorded defeat nor explicitly a CM-20-0330 cut.
challenging_evidence.source_title: City Council budget minutes, November 21–29, 2023, items 5.1.1–5.1.2
challenging_evidence.establishes: The destination in the text actually voted on and why the withdrawn amendment is not a third qualifying attempt.

limitations: The portal blocked direct access to full historical minutes. I checked the carried programme-related items for the required Council meetings beginning November 30, 2022; March 14 and April 17, 2023; November 21–29, 2023; December 2–5, 2024; August 19 and September 16–17, 2025; and the carried June 30 and July 7, 2026 committee and Council items. The selection rule may omit a motion whose text did not identify the programme.
The carried extracts identify the multi-day meetings but do not date each amendment’s final vote within its meeting’s continuation days.
unknowns: Whether a differently worded programme-reduction motion appears in an uncarried item of a full Council minutes page.
what_would_change_my_verdict: A second defeated motion by either councillor that left $45 million to $55 million and named a destination would make the primary proposition Supported.
A contemporaneous approved-budget adjustment before the December 2024 motion large enough to put its remainder in that band would change the amount calculation.
claims.suggested_one_line: Principe and Rice backed two defeated programme cuts, but only the first would have left about $50 million; the second would have left $32.7 million.
claims.suggested_short_answer: The November 2023 motion sought a $50 million cut from a $100 million capital budget and lost 4–8. The December 2024 motion sought a $67.3 million cut from the same approved base and lost 4–7. Both specified reduced tax-supported debt funding.
